expectations.text: `runCatching` around a suspend call swallows CancellationException.
expectations.evidence: Finding #5: "runCatching around a suspend call captures CancellationException into Result.failure — so a cancelled latest() looks like a failed network call instead of propagating. The skill names this exactly ('Never wrap a suspend call in stdlib runCatching')."

expectations.text: Empty `catch (e: Exception) {}` in stream() swallows cancellation.
expectations.evidence: Finding #3: "catch (e: Exception) swallows CancellationException — the watchlist Flow cannot be cancelled... CancellationException is an Exception, so this catch eats it and the loop keeps going... the loop never stops — a leaked coroutine still polling the gateway."

Finding #6: "a fresh Json { ... } builder is allocated on every latest() invocation. Each Json {} discards the per-class serializer/descriptor cache... Hoist one reused Json to a top-level/object val (or inject it)."

expectations.text: Returning cached/0.0 on failure masks the outage; 0.0 sentinel dangerous.
expectations.evidence: Finding #5: "Returning a default on failure masks outages. On a real network error this returns the stale cached price, or 0.0 if the symbol was never cached. A 0.0 price silently flowing into a trading watchlist / alerts service is a correctness-and-money bug... the alerts service could fire on a fake zero."
Finding #4: "GlobalScope.launch in prefetch() — orphaned, uncancellable, untestable work... GlobalScope work has no parent, is never cancelled, and outlives any caller."

expectations.text: Hardcoded `Dispatchers.IO` hurts testability (should be injected) -- NOT praising it.
expectations.evidence: Finding #8: "Hardcoded Dispatchers.IO inside the class... Nondeterministic and untestable — runTest's virtual time can't drive it, and you can't substitute a test dispatcher. The skill requires injecting the dispatcher with a prod default. Fix: Constructor-inject private val io: CoroutineDispatcher = Dispatchers.IO." Treated as a defect, not praised.

expectations.text: `accumulated += chunk` + re-split as O(n^2) / re-emitting old lines (freeze symptom).
expectations.evidence: Finding #2: "accumulated += chunk then for (line in accumulated.split('\n'))... every loop re-splits and re-emits all prices seen since the stream opened... O(n²) re-scan + unbounded memory... += on a String accumulator inside the loop is the GC-pressure anti-pattern."

Finding #1: "stream() busy-loops with no delay, hammering the endpoint and starving the dispatcher... while (true) { http.get(...).bodyAsText(); ... } with no delay() and no backoff... a polling loop needs a paced delay() and, on error, jittered capped backoff — never a free-running while(true)."

expectations.text: Frames the review EXPLICITLY at Tier 0 (states it's app/internal code, library tiers don't apply).
expectations.evidence: "Tier classification: Internal app data-layer class (com.acme.trading.data)... No published API surface, no commonMain/expect/actual, no publishing block. → Tier 0 (Core) only. I am deliberately not raising ABI / explicitApi / multiplatform / publishing concerns; they don't apply here." Explicit Tier-0 clause stating library tiers do not apply.

expectations.text: Raises NO explicitApi/ABI/publishing concerns (no tier-confusion false positives).
expectations.evidence: explicitApi/ABI/multiplatform/publishing are mentioned only to explicitly EXCLUDE them as not applicable ('I am deliberately not raising ABI / explicitApi / multiplatform / publishing concerns'). No tier-confusion false positives raised.

It explicitly classified the file as Tier 0 (internal app data-layer) and stated that ABI/explicitApi/multiplatform/publishing concerns do not apply — satisfying both the explicit tier-framing clause (#9) and the absence check (#10).
